destination.name: Waipoua Forest
whyVisit: See Tāne Mahuta, lord of the forest

slots.reason: See Tāne Mahuta, lord of the forest

slots.bio: The largest known living kauri tree, about 2,000 years old and over 50 metres tall.
slots.current: 00 29 0496 Waipoua Forest NZ - Kauri Baum Tane Mahuta.jpg

slots.bio: Father of the Forest, a huge kauri with the widest girth in the country, reached by a short bush walk.
A cluster of four kauri trees joined at the base, beside the road through the forest.
slots.override: Waipoua Forest, group of kauri trees (Four Sisters)-6.jpg
slots.current: Waipoua Forest, group of kauri trees (Four Sisters)-6.jpg

slots.bio: A long, tidal harbour with huge white sand dunes on the north head, reached by ferry or boat.
A harbourside village famous for Opo the friendly dolphin of the 1950s, with views over the dunes.
